subject: Cartwheel: client retry fallthrough causing 5xx/429 spike - urgent
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cartwheel.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T20:03:00Z
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood - appears tied to retries

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing an uptick in 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood for our API token (cartwheel-prod) at ~2026-11-01 19:40 UTC. Error rate jumped to ~14% on our production routes and our customers are complaining of timeouts. We rolled back to the previous SDK for a small slice and the error rate dropped immediately. We've attached a zip with short log snippets (request ids, timestamps, and response codes).

Quick context: we pushed an internal SDK update (cartwheel-js v2.3.0) yesterday that included a change to the retry helper. Some teams set the backoff param to 0 to reduce perceived latency on transient errors; we suspected this might be OK but now we see amplification.

Can Redwood help triage? We can be on a call.

Attachments: cartwheel_log_snippets.zip

Alex

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood - appears tied to retries

Thanks for the heads-up, Vanessa. I've pulled the token and short windows show repeated bursts of identical request patterns with inter-request spacing in sub-100ms ranges from a small set of client IPs. That is exactly what you see when clients remove exponential backoff and jitter.

Quick analysis / proposed mitigations (short-term):
1) Apply a per-token burst throttle: limit maximum request rate to 200 rps with a short token-level queue. This will blunt the amplification immediately.
2) Enable short-lived circuit breaker on routes returning 5xx/429 (open for 10s after 20% error rate spike).
3) Add a gateway-level heuristic to detect repeated identical Authorization token + path combos and delay/dampen retries for 2-5s (server-side backoff proxy).

I can roll 1 and 2 in the next 15-30 minutes as emergency config. We should prefer server-side dampening rather than dropping requests, to avoid data loss for legitimate traffic.

Longer-term: push a recommended SDK patch to cartwheel that enforces jitter and sane defaults (maxRetries=3, baseBackoff=200ms, jitter=0.3). Markus, engineering team should work with Cartwheel to validate their v2.3.1 with the fixes.

I'll start the emergency config now. Assigning myself to incident runbook.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Cartwheel incident

Alex / Maya — thanks again for your patience. Summary from our side:

Timeline:
- 2026-11-01 19:40 UTC: Cartwheel reports spike in 5xx/429.
- 2026-11-01 20:05 UTC: Redwood applied token-level burst throttle + route circuit-breaker (reduced error rate within 6 minutes).
- 2026-11-01 21:30 UTC: Cartwheel rolled back to previous SDK on a subset of services; further reduction observed.

Root cause (high level):
- Cartwheel SDK v2.3.0 introduced a change that allowed teams to set backoff=0 and removed jitter in some helper wrappers. That led to synchronized retries under transient failures and amplified load on Redwood service endpoints, which caused increased 5xx/429 and timeouts.

Actions completed:
- Emergency throttle and circuit-breaker applied (Rishi) — immediate mitigation.
- Support bridge and customer communication (Soojin / Vanessa).
- Eng to ship compliant SDK patch (Markus will coordinate).

Open / next steps:
- Cartwheel to publish v2.3.1 with enforced jitter and sane defaults (target: 2026-11-04).
- Redwood to add a short-lived server-side "retry dampener" for identical token+path combos (engineering to scope).
- Follow-up canary and post-mortem scheduled: 2026-11-05 14:00 UTC.

Impact & ask for exec awareness:
- Customer-facing impact: intermittent timeouts for several enterprise customers using Cartwheel; peak error rate ~14% but reduced to <1% after throttle.
- Business: Cartwheel is a mid-tier customer with an upcoming renewal in Q1; they escalated to their CTO during the incident.
- Ask for bandwidth: we may need a short-term exception to accelerate the server-side dampener rollout this week (Rishi / Markus).

We'll prepare a formal post-mortem for distribution after the canary. Please let me know if you'd like this escalated to GTM or exec review.

Best,
